description: Routes nine inputs to nine outputs, rearranging the routing on each clock by a rule the mode and entropy switches pick out of eighteen

params.text: Switches between treating the nine lines one at a time and treating them as pairs, so that each pair is moved together
Picks one of six families of rearrangement: Basic, Up, Down, Broadcast, Pairs and Triplets
Picks how far each clock moves the routing from where it is: Negative pulls it back towards straight through, Low makes a small change, and High makes a large one

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the rule the mode and entropy switches name
A rising edge past 1V puts the routing back to straight through, each input to the output of the same number
One of the nine signals to be routed; where it comes out depends on the routing as it stands
Replaces the channels switch, below 5V for one line at a time and 5V or above for pairs; with trigger mode on, a rising edge flips it instead
Replaces the mode switch, a voltage of 0V to 10V picking one of the six in order; with trigger mode on, a rising edge steps or jumps to another mode instead
Replaces the entropy switch, a voltage of 0V to 10V picking one of the three in order; with trigger mode on, a rising edge steps or jumps to another setting instead
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the negative rule of the current mode, whatever the entropy switch is set to
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the low rule of the current mode, whatever the entropy switch is set to
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the high rule of the current mode, whatever the entropy switch is set to

outputs.text: Carries whichever input the routing currently sends here, or a crossfade between the old and new ones while fading is switched on

notes: nothing happens until a clock arrives: the routing starts straight through and only a clock, or one of the three entropy clocks, changes it.
the eighteen rules are the six modes crossed with the three entropy settings: Basic gives Unwind, Swap and Randomize, and Up and Down give Sort, Shunt and Rotate in that direction.
Broadcast gives Split, Double and Blast, which set two or all nine outputs to the same input; Pairs and Triplets repeat the Basic rules in sets of two and three.
the three entropy clock inputs act alongside the main clock, so one patch can pull the routing about with one clock and settle it with another.
every output carries as many channels as the widest cable patched into any input.
menu: Trigger mode: Enabled, Random mode — turns the three CV jacks into trigger inputs that step through their settings, and Random mode inside it makes each trigger jump to a random setting instead
Hold last value — makes an output hold the last voltage it carried when the input the routing sends it is unpatched, instead of dropping to 0V
Fade while switching — crossfades between the old routing and the new one instead of switching at once
Fade Time — sets how long that crossfade takes
